SRC-218:R001.text: Provide one command or UI action that starts the authorized parallel worker pool for SAIPEN engineering. Source asks for one click or command. T-442 and T-443/T-444 admission remain required.

SRC-218:R002.text: SAIPEN assigns distinct eligible task or audit generations autonomously. Bind each assignment to exact Source bytes and one current owner; duplicate delivery cannot assign the same generation twice.

SRC-218:R003.text: Use separate Git worktrees for engineering workers, with separate indexes and bounded writable scope. Prove source isolation before concurrent edits. Source explicitly requests worktrees.

SRC-218:R004.text: Parallel workers perform actual engineering improvements to admitted SAIPEN tasks or audits and produce source patches. Read-only research or a toy arithmetic demonstration cannot satisfy this request.

SRC-218:R005.text: Proposed acceptance R5: each worker durably checkpoints identity, assignment generation, owned changes, verification status and remaining work independently of chat. Original source does not explicitly specify this recovery format.

SRC-218:R006.text: Proposed acceptance R6: worker loss, provider limit or restart preserves accepted work. This is a proposed operational completion criterion, not evidence that failover exists or authority to implement before admission.

SRC-218:R007.text: Proposed acceptance R7: a fresh replacement resumes the same assignment from durable verified progress without repeating unchanged completed checks. Prove an actual model-session restart after lawful admission.

SRC-218:R008.text: Engineering handbacks are immutable patch-and-evidence proposals bound to base source identity, worker, Work, declared resources and verification. Reuse ProducerPackage and the existing Core integration owners rather than creating an incompatible format.

SRC-218:R009.text: Refuse stale proposals and conflicting read/write or logical-resource claims before canonical mutation. Preserve refused proposals and their evidence; never silently rebase or merge changed dependencies.

SRC-218:R010.text: One canonical Core integrator accepts eligible proposals sequentially through the existing writer lock and journal. Workers do not become concurrent authors of canonical STATE, BOARD or LOG.

SRC-218:R011.text: Each accepted engineering proposal requires independent verification on the relevant source generation and the mandatory integration gates. A worker cannot approve its own handback or replace complete required regression coverage with focused tests.

SRC-218:R012.text: Consume an audit only through exact-generation Source closure and the canonical audit delete gate after linked Work is terminal. Patch acceptance alone never authorizes Source deletion.
